text:
Maya: Quick thread — ran a focused sweep comparing streaming (SSE + WebSocket) vs non-streaming HTTP/polling across us-west1 and eu-central on A100 / A10G. TL;DR: streaming (SSE) gives higher max throughput with batching, WebSocket gives lower tail latency for small requests. Chart + raw CSV: https://tiny.redwood/dualpath-sweep :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Alex: can you paste the summary numbers here?

Maya: sure, pasted the condensed CSV below for quick eyeballing:
```
region,gpu,endpoint,p50(ms),p99(ms),max_rps
us-west1,A100,websocket,58,240,420
us-west1,A100,sse,75,310,560
us-west1,A100,http-poll,45,200,320
eu-central,A10G,websocket,72,320,300
eu-central,A10G,sse,90,420,430
eu-central,A10G,http-poll,55,280,260
```

Sam: interesting — SSE has much higher max_rps on A100 (560) vs WS (420). were you using persistent connections for WS in this run?

Maya: yes, WS was persistent connections + small-message mode. SSE used chunked transfer with server-side batching + prefix caching. HTTP-poll was single-shot requests with minimal batching (to represent PLG traffic).

Jin: what kernels/configs were used?

Maya: A100 runs flash-attn2 + fused KV ops; A10G fell back to Triton attention kernels for a few layers so perf less ideal. Quantization: A10G test used 4-bit q4_k_m for cost realism; A100 kept fp16 for high-throughput baseline.

Rachel: any quality regressions from the 4-bit run?

Maya: tiny regressions on our instr/rouge set — ~0.6-0.9% lower on targeted prompts. flagged in the eval dashboard, nothing catastrophic but worth tracking for customer-impact prompts.

ops-bot: deploy: load-test/canary group started (canary-23)

Alex: notes for runbook: for latency-sensitive <100 token requests prefer websocket on A100 (lower p10/p50), for throughput-heavy batchy workloads SSE on A100 wins cost/RPS. On A10G the delta compresses — SSE still better for throughput but latency penalty larger. Document kernel + quant knobs: flash-attn / fused-kv for A100, avoid aggressive 4-bit unless evals pass.

Sam: can you add p50 vs RPS curves and cold vs warm KV cache runs? Those will help sizing for Dedicated pools.

Maya: added curves in the chart link; warm KV cache reduced p50 by ~15-22ms for streaming; cold starts hit that p99 spike on SSE (cache miss heatups).

Jin: SGTM. recommend a 15m sync to pick defaults for Dedicated sizing and kernel/quant presets. Pinged @ops-bot to propose times.

deploy-bot: calendar: quick-sync scheduled 2026-04-02 14:00 UTC (15m)

Alex: perfect — thanks Maya. will add summary to the onboarding checklist (kernel+quant note + preferred endpoints by workload). :thumbsup:

Maya: moving next to a long-tail prompt eval and a repeat with A100 q4-int8 mix for cost sensitivity. will post results in the same thread.
